content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Compound and Multi-Key Indexes in NoSQL Databases"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In modern NoSQL databases, efficient data retrieval is paramount for scalability. While single-field indexes work well for basic queries, real-world applications frequently filter by multiple criteria or query nested arrays. This tutorial explores compound indexes and multi-key indexes, explaining how they optimize complex data access patterns."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Compound Indexes"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A compound index is a single index structure that holds references to multiple fields within a collection's documents. They allow databases to efficiently resolve queries that filter or sort by more than one field."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"The ESR Rule for Compound Indexes"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"When designing compound indexes, following the Equality, Sort, Range (ESR) rule ensures optimal performance:"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Equality: Place fields that you query for exact matches first in the index."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Sort: Place fields used for sorting next, bridging the gap between equality and range conditions."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Range: Place fields that require range evaluations (like greater than or less than) last."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"db.orders.createIndex({ status: 1, orderDate: -1, totalAmount: 1 })"},{"order":11,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Multi-Key Indexes"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"NoSQL databases frequently store data as arrays. To index fields inside an array, databases use multi-key indexes. When you create an index on a field that contains an array, the database automatically creates separate index entries for each element of the array."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"db.products.createIndex({ tags: 1 })"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"If a document contains {\"tags\": [\"electronics\", \"sale\", \"featured\"]}, the multi-key index will create three distinct index entries pointing to that single document ID."},{"order":15,"type":"heading","text":"Combining Compound and Multi-Key Indexes"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can combine both concepts to create a compound multi-key index. This occurs when a compound index includes one or more fields that are arrays. While powerful, these indexes come with specific performance constraints."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A compound index can only contain one array field. If you attempt to index multiple fields that are arrays, the database will return an error."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Multi-key indexes can increase index size significantly because a single document can generate many index keys depending on the array length."},{"order":19,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering compound and multi-key indexes enables you to build high-performance NoSQL data models. By strategically applying the ESR rule and managing array-based fields carefully, you ensure your queries scale efficiently as your dataset grows."}]
